solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Obtained directly from leading worker

parts.note: leading means first, ahead of the rest
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Something learned straight from the top employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Firsthand knowledge comes straight from the source, with no intermediary between it and you.

clue.text: Viral infection following repeatedly will get you down

parts.note: flu, influenza, is a viral infection

indicators.note: repeatedly tells us the abbreviation for the word beside it is used twice

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Catching a virus again and again will make you feel low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like a mood, the result of being ill, but it is the soft feathery stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Down and fluff are both soft light fibres, such as the first feathers of a chick.

clue.text: Agent involved in the preparations

indicators.note: involved in signals letters lying inside the next word, enclosed by it

explanation.surface: A representative takes part in getting things ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A rep, a sales representative, acts as an agent for a company.

clue.text: Not an easy situation for a drunk to be in

definitions.text: Not an easy situation for a drunk to be in

parts.words: Not an easy situation for a drunk to be in
parts.note: reads as a tricky predicament, while also hinting at a drunk person, who is tight, standing somewhere

explanation.surface: A difficult position that a drinker might find himself in.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight is old slang for drunk, so the drunk is 'tight' in a 'spot' as well as in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight spot is an idiom for an awkward predicament that is hard to escape.

clue.text: Sherry lover

definitions.meaning: a medium sweet style of sherry from Spain
the Spanish and Italian word for a lover or sweetheart

explanation.definitionFit: Amoroso names a sweetened oloroso sherry and, in Italian and Spanish, a lover.

clue.text: I posted another payment after this

indicators.note: another version of the letters gives a different word from the same set

explanation.surface: A note that the writer mailed a further instalment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' rearranges I POSTED; the definition is a payment that is followed by further payments, as when buying in instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is the initial sum paid down, with the balance to follow later.

clue.text: Bill about land

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: An invoice relating to a plot of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land measuring 4,840 square yards.

clue.text: Poor creature among the pews

parts.note: a small animal living in a place of worship, proverbial for having nothing to eat

explanation.surface: A pitiful animal scurrying in a chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' is meant literally: the saying 'as poor as a church mouse' describes someone penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'poor as a church mouse' makes this creature the emblem of poverty.

clue.text: Always ten really confused

indicators.note: confused means the letters of the words beside it are muddled up

explanation.surface: A complaint that ten is forever genuinely bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means forever, at all times without end.

clue.text: Gloomy linesman on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a bard is a poet, a writer of lines

explanation.surface: A downcast football official climbing upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linesman' suggests a football referee's assistant but is a poet who writes lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab means dull and dreary, much as gloomy does.

clue.text: Release a Parisian woman

parts.note: un is the French word for a, as spoken in Paris
Peg is a woman's name, short for Margaret

explanation.surface: Let a French lady go free.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpeg is to unfasten or free something held by a peg, hence release it.

clue.text: Work quietly on alternative melody conveniently presented

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
or introduces an alternative
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: Writing a soft piece on a different air that arrives at just the right time.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune describes something arriving at a well-timed, convenient moment.

clue.text: Disagreeing about one point whilst trying to be amusing

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the next one

parts.note: factious means quarrelsome, prone to dissent
E, east, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Arguing over a single detail while attempting humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Facetious describes flippant remarks made in an attempt at humour.

clue.text: What bather is doing admitting it

definitions.meaning: a bather in the bath is getting washed, emerging spotless
owning up to the truth, making a confession

explanation.definitionFit: Coming clean is an idiom for confessing, and literally a bather becomes clean.

clue.text: Danish essayist?

definitions.meaning: Denmark is famous for its cured pork rashers
Francis ..., the Elizabethan philosopher, wrote celebrated essays

explanation.definitionFit: Danish bacon is a well-known breakfast meat, and Bacon was an English essayist.

clue.text: Sportsman on half-pay?

parts.note: an athlete who is only partly a paid player, as if half of a professional

explanation.surface: An athlete receiving only half his wages.
explanation.walkthrough: Semi means half, so a part-time professional is pictured as one on half pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-pro plays sport for money but not as a full-time career.

clue.text: Odds on Leonard with sullen brilliance

parts.note: SP, starting price, gives the betting odds in racing
Len is short for Leonard
dour means sullen, stern

explanation.surface: A bet placed on a gloomy man called Leonard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds' looks like alternate letters but is SP, the starting price at a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour means magnificence or brilliance of appearance.

clue.text: Current uprising

parts.note: reads as a present-day revolt, but describes a flow of air that goes up

explanation.surface: A revolt happening now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests 'present-day' and 'uprising' a revolt; in fact it is an air current that rises.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermal is a column of warm rising air used by gliders and birds.

clue.text: Wrongly sent in before due time in a serious way

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged word goes inside the other piece

parts.note: early means before the expected time

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of the next word are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly submitted something ahead of a deadline, quite solemnly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' looks like it qualifies 'sent' in the surface, but it signals the rearrangement, and 'in' places the result inside the synonym of 'before due time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnestly means sincerely and seriously, with intense conviction.

clue.text: New driver in Connecticut used half the medicine

parts.note: L, learner, is the plate on a new driver's car in Britain
CT is the postal abbreviation for Connecticut

indicators.note: half the tells us only the first two of the four letters of the following word are taken

explanation.surface: A learner motorist in New England took half the drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'in' gives its own letters rather than signalling a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Linctus is a syrupy cough medicine.

clue.text: Close space made by temporary substitute

parts.note: to stop something is to close it, as with a hole
a gap is a space

explanation.surface: Shutting a hole with a makeshift fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary measure used until something better arrives.

clue.text: False swearing according to panel

parts.note: per means according to, as in 'per instructions'
a jury is a panel of citizens

explanation.surface: Lying under oath, as the jurors saw it.
explanation.definitionFit: Perjury is the crime of lying under oath in court.

clue.text: Worst place to park during break for repairs

parts.note: the pits means the worst, in slang
P is the map and road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A dreadful parking spot during a mechanical stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' acts as a link meaning 'put': PITS, then TO, then P for park.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit stop is a halt in motor racing for refuelling and repairs.

clue.text: Northern Ireland certainly a third more pleasant

indicators.note: a third means the opening third of the nine-letter word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: Ulster is definitely a bit nicer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer is the comparative of nice, meaning more agreeable or pleasant.

clue.text: Man who's born-again?

parts.note: a man's name whose French meaning is reborn

explanation.surface: A fellow converted to evangelical faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The French name René literally means reborn.
explanation.definitionFit: René is a man's name derived from Latin renatus, meaning born again.

clue.text: Need month off recovering

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone requires a month's leave to recuperate.
explanation.definitionFit: On the mend is an idiom for getting better after illness.

clue.text: Alien had many a coin from Albania

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number
the lek is the currency of Albania

explanation.surface: A foreigner possessed lots of Albanian money.
explanation.walkthrough: A Dalek is an alien from the British TV series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: Daleks are the robotic extraterrestrial villains of Doctor Who.

clue.text: Voting her out during a dark period

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the words are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: She is elected or ejected during the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnight means during the night, the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Whole drink taken to health centre

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A complete drink taken to the clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'health centre' looks like a clinic; it means the middle letters of 'health'.
explanation.definitionFit: Total means complete or whole.

clue.text: Modest woman's figure?

parts.note: figure as a number: a modest woman would wear a ...-piece rather than skimpier swimwear

explanation.surface: The shape of a demure lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' pretends to be a body shape but is a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Two is a figure, a number, here linked to a modest two-piece costume.

clue.text: Class row

definitions.meaning: a grade or standing in a hierarchy
a line of soldiers or things side by side

explanation.definitionFit: Rank means a class or grade, and also a line, as in rank and file.

clue.text: Rubbish, it produces opium, mate

parts.note: opium comes from the poppy plant
cock is a British form of address for a friend, as in 'wotcha, cock'

explanation.surface: Nonsense about the drug-yielding flower and a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppycock is slang for nonsense or rubbish.
